title: What is known about 1RB1LD_1LC---_1RE0LD_1LC1LD_1RF0RE_1RA0RC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LD_1LC---_1RE0LD_1LC1LD_1RF0RE_1RA0RC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: Open. The same kind of structure as 1RB0RA_1LC0RC_1LF0RD_1RA1LE_0LC---_1LD0LA: long blocks of a repeated word separated by digit-like separators that change near the left end every sweep and carry to the right.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 35,704 cells have been visited and 17,923 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: power/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.181).

claims.title: The structure of the run
claims.text: Bouncer growing to the left: blocks of the word 10 separated by short separators (110, 0, 11 110, ...) that act as counter digits; the first block grows steadily, block lengths fall off to the right.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. No closed rule set has been found; see the README for what a proof would need.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB0RD_1RC1LE_1LD---_1RF0LE_1LD1LE_1RA0RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. This page runs the machine in your browser and describes the structure seen in its run.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 35,704 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
bouncer with a multi-digit counter of 10 blocks (chaotic)

sections.heading: What the tape looks like
html: Read from the left end, the tape is blocks of a = 10 separated by separators such as b = 110, 0, 1 1 b. The separators near the left end change at each sweep and carry to the right like counter digits; the first block grows by about one a per sweep. The left end grows 2 cells per sweep; the right end moves out only 579 times in 109 steps.

sections.heading: Where it could halt
html: The only halting transition is B reading 1. A closed tape language with windows of 6 cells (bbtools.ctl) covers the run but still allows halts, with only a local constraint near the head: the cells left of the head read (outward) 111000, 111001, 111010 or 111101. Nothing confines a halt to an edge.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.514). Right of the start it grows like a power of the step count other than 1/2 (fitted exponent 0.181).
After 109 steps the tape spans 35,704 cells (23,962 left of the start, 2,389 right), with a density of 1s of 0.502.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machine below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in the other, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
